claim.title: Rule-30 CA learning exhibits grokking
claim.statement: Training a tensor-network student model to learn the Rule-30 cellular automaton rule exhibits grokking, characterized by a sudden drop in test error to zero after a period of high test error following zero training error.
claim.test_plan: Implement the tensor-network attention model described in Section 4.2. Generate training data for the Rule-30 CA (K=1 local rule) with sequence length $M=100$. Train the model using gradient descent with weight decay. Monitor training and test error. Pass if there exists a time interval where training error is 0 (or near 0) but test error is $> 0.5$, followed by a rapid drop in test error to $< 0.05$.
claim.evidence_in_paper: Section 4.3: 'We numerically study grokking... on the example of learning a 1D rule-30 cellular automaton... We show that sudden spikes in the training loss correspond to structural changes...'
claim.success_criterion: The training curve exhibits a phase where train error is $\approx 0$ and test error is $> 0.5$, followed by a transition to test error $< 0.05$.
